why: The student wrote a correct index-based loop, a[i] = a[i] * 10, which repairs the given for-each loop that never changed the array. This is the familiar canonical traversal with no reasoning beyond the given code, so it is L3 rather than L4.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) a[i] = a[i] * 10;
concepts.why: The loop variable is used as the index, so each pass writes a different element; the run gives [50, 40, 30, 20, 10].
The same expression a[i] reads and writes a different element on each pass of the loop.
The for header gives i each valid index 0..length-1 once, the standard way to process every element.
a.length is used correctly as a field without parentheses, but nothing more is said about it.
i++ is used correctly as the loop update with no explanation.
The answer makes no claim about the for-each loop.
